Documentation style guide ¶ What every Kokeb Labs documentation site contains, how its pages are written and what a README looks like. The pilot site, kokeb-labs/driver-tmc9660 , follows every rule here; copy its structure. Voice ¶ Plain and specific. "SPI mode 3, up to 10 MHz", not "supports high-speed SPI". Numbers, names, units. Second person, present tense, active voice. "Call init() before anything else", not "The init function should be called". Short sentences. One idea each. A paragraph is three to five sentences. No hype, no filler. No "simply", "just", "easily", "powerful", "comprehensive", "seamless", "robust". No emoji in headings, lists or tables. No walls of bold. No exclamation marks. Sentence case for titles and headings: "Bus settings", not "Bus Settings". British or American spelling : either, consistently within a repository. True statements only. Every API name, signature, pin, register and number is checked against the headers or the datasheet. When something is derived rather than measured, say so. Never mention how the page was produced. No "generated by", no tool or assistant names. Every page ¶ A title ( # Title , level one, exactly one), matching its navigation entry. A purpose line right under it: one sentence saying what the reader gets from the page. The theme renders it as the lead paragraph. Sections ( ## ) in the order a reader needs them. A section that is only a link list belongs in a table or in the navigation instead. A next step when there is an obvious one ( Next: [Porting](porting.md) ). No Jekyll front matter, no Liquid. Material front matter is allowed only for hide: (the home page hides the navigation and table of contents). Components ¶ The theme styles these; use them instead of inventing markup. Need Write Notes A warning that prevents damage or lost hours !!! warning "Title" / !!! danger At most two per page. note , tip , example for the rest Optional detail ??? note "Title" Collapsed by default Alternatives (SPI / UART, ESP-IDF / CMake) === "SPI" tabs Same structure in each tab Code fenced block with a language; title="file.cpp" for a file Code from a compiled file: --8<-- "tests/docs/x.cpp:section" Registers, parameters, pins, options a table Header row, units in the header, code font for names Bit fields a table inside
Offset and name columns get code font Sequence or state machine a mermaid fence Themed for light and dark automatically Architecture, signal flow, layouts a figkit figure Light and dark from one layout, checked for contrast A light-only image (vendor SVG, photo) ![alt](x.svg){ .kb-plate } Sits on a white plate in dark mode Steps

Home page; four to six cards Chip card ¶
Smart gate driver with on-chip FOC TMC9660 Analog Devices (Trinamic)
Interface : SPI mode 3 up to 10 MHz, or UART Supply : 7.7 V to 70 V [ Datasheet ]( datasheet/tmc9660.pdf ) · [ Reference manual ]( datasheet/ref.pdf )
Five to seven rows: function, interface (mode, speed, address), supply, key limits, package, and the mode the driver uses. A board uses class="kb-chip kb-chip--board" with MCU, power input, connectors, chips on board. Code ¶ It compiles against the real API. In a C++ repository, every snippet longer than one line lives in build (an OBJECT library, warnings on) and is included in the page with --8<-- "tests/docs/x.cpp:name" . Instantiate the driver template over the documented port so the whole API is compiled. It is the smallest complete thing. Includes, the object, the calls, the error check. No // ... in a block that claims to be complete. It checks results. Every driver call returns a status: show what to do with it. Names are real. A reader can paste them. One-line inline names ( setTargetVelocityRpm() ) are checked by searching the headers. The README quickstart is a generated region ( ) copied from the same compiled file, so it cannot drift. Figures ¶ figkit for architecture and anything drawn from the code: one module per figure in docs/diagrams/figures/.py , data() reads the facts from the headers, build() lays out cards. The build refuses text under 4.5:1 contrast in either theme, overlaps and missing alt text; kokeb-docs figures --check fails CI when the code changed and the figure did not. Embed with / . Mermaid for sequences and state machines. How a figure reads ¶ Most confusing diagrams mix up what an arrow means or which way to read. Every figure follows these rules: One reading direction, said in the subtitle. Top to bottom for layers and calls, left to right for steps in time. When two things happen at different times (a push and a tag), draw two lanes, one per trigger, each with its trigger as the lane title. Every arrow is a verb. Solid arrows run or call something; dashed arrows carry data (a file, an artifact, a setting). Label an arrow whenever the verb isn't obvious from the legend ( uploads , reads , forwards to your hooks ). An arrow points from the one acting to the one acted on. Colour is ownership, three tones at most. teal is what the reader writes or owns, brand is this repository, slate is outside (hardware, GitHub, ESP-IDF). Draw owned cards with accent=True so they match the legend swatches. Add ("~solid", ...) and ("~dashed", ...) to the legend when both arrow kinds appear. Few boxes, short text. At most about eight cards, a title and one or two short lines each. Lists that come from the code (public calls, commands) go in chips inside a region. Say the point. The subtitle states the one thing the reader should take away; a note answers the question the figure raises (for example, why the release does not rebuild). Vendor diagrams only as SVG or compressed PNG, with { .kb-plate } , never screenshots of PDFs. Alt text on every image: one sentence that says what the figure shows, not "diagram". The build fails on a missing alt. PDFs (datasheets, manuals) live in docs/datasheet/ and are linked, never embedded; the site links them on GitHub, which renders them. Tables ¶ Use a table whenever there are three or more items with the same attributes: pins, registers, parameters, options, commands, error codes, compile-time switches. Put units in the header ( Range (V) ), names in code font, and keep cells short; long prose goes under the table. Links ¶ Link pages by file ( [Porting](porting.md#threads) ); MkDocs checks them in strict mode. Link repository files relatively ( [`inc/x.hpp`](../inc/x.hpp) ); the plugin turns them into GitHub links at the commit that was built. Link the API reference with api/...html ; the link check verifies it after Doxygen is merged. External links go to the primary source (vendor page, datasheet, specification). Standard page sets ¶ Driver ( driver-* ) ¶ Page File Contains Home index.md Hero (what, one-sentence why, buttons), the "no platform code" paragraph, chip card, "What you get" (5-7 bullets, each linking its page), navigation cards Quickstart quickstart.md Safety note if it moves hardware; wiring table; add the driver; the port (compiled); a ~15-line example (compiled); what each step does; a "if it does not work" table Installation installation.md Requirements; submodule; CMake target and options; ESP-IDF component; build layout; version; compile-time switches Hardware hardware.md Pin table(s) with directions; control pins; bus settings table (mode, speed, frame, timing); a timing diagram or Mermaid sequence for the protocol; power ranges; errata that affect the host; evaluation boards; reference documents table Architecture architecture.md The layer figure (core, communication interface, platform port); a table of layers with files; one call traced through the layers (Mermaid); design choices (CRTP, no heap); source map API guide api-guide.md Task-oriented, compiled snippets: the shape of the API (subsystems table); initialise; configure; read; write; batch or stream if any; raw register / parameter access; errors and faults (a table of signals); tuning API reference api-reference.md Button to api/index.html ; a "start here" table of the five most useful Doxygen pages Examples examples.md (from examples/*/app_config.yml ); one-time setup; "what to read in an example" table Porting porting.md The interface methods table with contracts; the port for each bus (compiled); rules for the transfer; control-pin levels; reference implementation; how to check a port; threads Testing and CI testing.md Host tests (how to run, what each file covers); compiled snippets; CI workflows table; hardware tests Troubleshooting troubleshooting.md Symptom, cause, fix; start with the cheapest check Changelog changelog.md # Changelog , a purpose line and --8<-- "CHANGELOG.md:N" (from the line after the file's own title) Figures diagrams/index.md Written by kokeb-docs figures Deep-dive pages (bootloader, protocols, timing, units, calibration) go under Concepts ; configuration references under Guides . Navigation ( docs/.nav.yml ) is always five tabs: nav : - Home : index.md - Get started : [ Quickstart , Installation , Hardware ] - Concepts : [ Architecture , deep dives ... ] - Guides : [ API guide , Configuration , Porting , Examples , Troubleshooting ] - Reference : [ API reference , Testing and CI , Figures , Changelog ] Core library ( kb-core ) ¶ Home (hero, what problem it solves, a feature list, a "used by" table), Quickstart (smallest use), Concepts (the model the library implements, with a figure), API guide (by task), API reference, Integration (CMake / ESP-IDF, configuration macros), Testing and CI, Changelog. A utilities collection gets one page per utility under Guides, each with purpose, a compiled example and complexity or memory notes. Board support (HAL) repositories ¶ Home with a board card ( kb-chip kb-chip--board ): MCU, power, connectors, chips on board; Quickstart (flash an example, see output); Hardware (block diagram figure, pin map as a generated table from the pin configuration, connectors, power tree); Architecture (managers, how drivers are wired, figure); one guide page per board function; API reference; Examples; Bring-up and troubleshooting; Changelog. Firmware products ¶ Home (what the product does, a photo or render with alt text, status), Getting started (flash, connect, first run), Architecture (tasks, data flow, figures), Operation (modes, commands, configuration), Hardware (link the HAL site), Development (build, test, release), Troubleshooting, Changelog. Decisions as ADRs under Reference. CI and tool repositories ( ci-tools , espidf-tools ) ¶ Home (what it provides, a table of workflows or scripts), Quickstart (the smallest caller), one page per workflow or script (purpose, jobs and permissions, inputs table generated from the YAML, example caller, failure modes), Versioning, Migration guides, Changelog. Organisation ( .github , kokeb-labs.github.io ) ¶ The portal ( kokeb-labs.github.io ) is the org home: what Kokeb Labs is, a card per product and HAL, a table of every driver with its chip, bus and docs link, and contribution links. .github holds the profile README following the README standard, plus community files. README standard ¶ The README is the front door on GitHub. It is short and points to the site. # Name and a hero line : one sentence, what it is and what it does. Badges that are true , in this order, only those that exist: CI (the main test workflow, branch=main ), docs (the docs workflow, linking the site), license, latest release (only once a release exists). No coverage badge without coverage, no "PRs welcome", no badge for a language version. The documentation link in bold. One diagram : the layer or block figure (figkit marker). A 30-second example : the generated quickstart region. What it does : five to seven bullets. Install : the submodule line and the CMake lines. Documentation : a table of the five or six most useful pages, linked to the site ( /latest/... ). Tests : one command line. License : one line. No table of contents, no walls of emoji, no feature lists with check marks, no badges that link nowhere, no duplicated API tables (that is the site's job). Checks that enforce this ¶ Check Where Fails on mkdocs build --strict PR CI broken links and anchors, pages missing from the nav, no H1, Jekyll front matter, Liquid, a page colliding with api/ , an image without alt text or file kokeb-docs check PR CI a figure or generated region that no longer matches the code Host build of tests/docs/ PR CI (repository) a snippet that does not compile lychee offline PR CI a broken link or anchor in the built site, API included Lighthouse PR CI performance, accessibility, best practices or SEO under budget markdownlint PR CI (repository) Markdown style

docs.text: Migrating a repository to MkDocs ¶ Move one repository's documentation from the Jekyll (just-the-docs) site to the Kokeb Labs MkDocs platform, from a clean checkout to a published, versioned site. Plan on half a day for a driver: the mechanical part takes minutes, the rest is rewriting pages to the style guide . The pilot is kokeb-labs/driver-tmc9660 : when a step is unclear, look at what that repository does. What the platform gives a repository ¶ Piece Where it lives The repository keeps Theme: brand, layout, header, footer, version selector, components packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme ( theme: kokeb ) nothing Plugin: Markdown dialect, validation, link rewriting, figure embeds, page checks same package ( plugins: [kokeb] ) nothing figkit and generated regions ( kokeb-docs figures , kokeb-docs gen ) same package figure modules under docs/diagrams/figures/ , optional generators under tools/docs/generators/ Toolchain (mkdocs, mkdocs-material, awesome-nav, pymdown, mike) pinned by the package nothing Build, checks, Doxygen, link check, Lighthouse, screenshots, publish ru-mkdocs-publish.yml a 30-line caller The workflow installs the package from the same commit as itself, so a caller pinned to @v1 always gets the theme released with v1 . A repository never carries CSS, templates, hooks or a requirements file for the site. The repository contract ¶ After migration a repository has exactly these documentation files: mkdocs.yml site name, description, repo_url, theme: kokeb, three plugins Doxyfile moved from _config/, OUTPUT_DIRECTORY = build/doxygen, no custom CSS docs/.nav.yml the navigation docs/*.md pages: plain Markdown, no Jekyll front matter, no Liquid docs/diagrams/figures/*.py figkit figure modules (optional) and their generated SVGs docs/datasheet/*.pdf linked, never rendered (the site links them on GitHub) docs/_doxygen/mainpage.md Doxygen main page (optional) tests/docs/*.cpp code shown on the pages, compiled by the host build (drivers) tools/docs/generators/*.py repository-specific generated regions (optional) .github/workflows/ci-docs-publish.yml Everything Jekyll is gone: _config/_config.yml , _config/_includes/ , _config/_layouts/ , _config/assets/ , _config/404.html , Gemfile* , docs/version_selector* , Liquid raw / endraw tags and the doxygen-awesome-css submodule. _config/ keeps the lint configurations ( .markdownlint.json , .yamllint , .clang-* , lychee.toml ). Steps ¶ 1. Branch and install ¶ git clone https://github.com/kokeb-labs/<repo>.git && cd <repo> git switch -c docs/mkdocs-platform python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate pip install "git+https://github.com/kokeb-labs/ci-tools@v1#subdirectory=packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme" Use @main (or the branch under review) instead of @v1 until the platform release that contains the package is out. 2. Run the mechanical migration ¶ python3 path/to/ci-tools/tools/docs-migrate.py . --check # the plan; changes nothing python3 path/to/ci-tools/tools/docs-migrate.py . --name "TMC9660 Driver" \ --description "One sentence on what this is." git add -A && git commit -m "Docs: move the site files to the MkDocs platform" The script strips front matter (adding # Title where a page had none), removes Liquid raw tags, drops emoji from headings and rewrites the anchors that changed, writes docs/.nav.yml from nav_order / parent , moves and cleans the Doxyfile, removes the doxygen-awesome submodule, writes mkdocs.yml and the caller workflow and deletes the Jekyll files. It also strips front matter from README files elsewhere in the repository. Run --check again: it must print already migrated . 3. Build ¶ mkdocs build --strict Fix every warning: strict mode turns them into failures, in CI too. The usual ones: Warning Fix contains a link 'x.md', but the target is not found The page was renamed; fix the link unrecognized relative link 'folder/' Link a file, or the folder is fine once it exists outside docs/ (the plugin links it on GitHub) no level-one heading Start the page with # Title Jekyll front matter / Liquid tag Remove it (the migration missed a file outside docs/ ?) builds to api/... A page named api.md collides with the Doxygen output: call it api-reference.md image(s) have no alt text Every image needs alt text 4. Rewrite the pages to the style guide ¶ Follow DOCS-STYLE-GUIDE.md : the standard page set for the repository type, a purpose line under every title, task-oriented API guide, verified code, a figure for the architecture, tables for registers. For a driver: Rename pages to the standard set ( hardware.md , porting.md , api-guide.md , ...) and rewrite .nav.yml into the five tabs (Home, Get started, Concepts, Guides, Reference). Put every C++ snippet in tests/docs/*.cpp , add them to an OBJECT library in tests/CMakeLists.txt (see the pilot), and include them with --8<-- "tests/docs/file.cpp:section" . Build it. Draw the layer figure with figkit ( docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py , reading class names from the headers) and run kokeb-docs figures . Fill the example table with <!-- generated: examples --> and run kokeb-docs gen . Rewrite the README to the README standard. 5. Doxygen ¶ The workflow runs Doxygen from the repository root with the Doxyfile and merges the HTML under api/ . OUTPUT_DIRECTORY = build/doxygen , HTML_OUTPUT = html (the workflow creates the folder). No HTML_EXTRA_STYLESHEET : the workflow then adds the Kokeb Labs API stylesheet and HTML_COLORSTYLE = AUTO_LIGHT . CASE_SENSE_NAMES = NO , so page names are the same on every OS ( classns_1_1_my_class.html ) and links from the site stay valid. GENERATE_TAGFILE empty; INPUT the headers (and src/ ), not the examples. A main page in docs/_doxygen/mainpage.md ( USE_MDFILE_AS_MAINPAGE ), not the README (badges and pictures break inside Doxygen). Check it locally the way CI does, then run the link check on the merged result: mkdir -p build/doxygen && doxygen Doxyfile mkdocs build --strict -d /tmp/site && mkdir -p /tmp/site/api && cp -a build/doxygen/html/. /tmp/site/api/ lychee --offline --include-fragments --index-files index.html --root-dir /tmp/site '/tmp/site/**/*.html' 6. Lint and look ¶ kokeb-docs check # figures and generated regions current npx markdownlint-cli2 --config _config/.markdownlint.json "docs/**/*.md" "*.md" pip install "kokeb-mkdocs-theme[screenshots] @ git+https://github.com/kokeb-labs/ci-tools@v1#subdirectory=packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme" playwright install chromium kokeb-docs screenshots /tmp/site /tmp/shots # 375 and 1280 px, light and dark Add "MD033": false (or allow the theme's HTML elements), "MD046": false and "MD041": false to _config/.markdownlint.json : pages use Material components and indented admonition bodies. Open the screenshots and read every page on the phone size. 7. Pull request ¶ Commit in small steps (site files; page rewrite; snippets and CMake; README) and open the pull request. CI must be green: the docs job runs the strict build, the drift checks, Doxygen, the offline link check, the Lighthouse budget, and uploads docs-site , lighthouse-report and docs-screenshots artifacts. Look at the screenshots artifact before asking for review. gh-pages and GitHub Pages ¶ The first publish replaces the old site ¶ The first push to main after the merge publishes version dev with mike. In the same run, before mike writes, the workflow removes every top-level entry of gh-pages that is not a mike version or alias (the Jekyll site's development/ , doxs/ , html/ , index.md , version_selector.html , ...) in one ordinary commit, "Remove the previous documentation site". Nothing is force-pushed. Kept: versions.json , mike's root index.html , .nojekyll , CNAME , robots.txt . The root index.html then redirects to latest/ , and a root 404.html sends old addresses ( /repo/docs/quickstart/ , /repo/doxs/... , /repo/html/... ) to the same page under latest/ (and Doxygen pages under latest/api/ ). A repository with no gh-pages branch at all gets one from mike on the first publish. Turn the cleanup off with prune_legacy: false if a repository keeps hand-made files at the top of gh-pages . Versions ¶ Event Version published Aliases Push to main dev latest , until the first release Tag vX.Y.Z vX.Y.Z ( release_version: minor publishes X.Y ) latest moves to it Pull request nothing The header shows the version selector; older versions show a banner linking to the latest. Pages settings (owner, once per repository) ¶ Settings > Pages > Build and deployment : Source Deploy from a branch , branch gh-pages , folder / . Every Kokeb Labs repository on the Jekyll pipeline already uses this, so usually nothing changes. A repository set to GitHub Actions as the source would never show the mike site: switch it to the branch. Check after the first publish: gh api repos/kokeb-labs/<repo>/pages --jq '.build_type, .source' # legacy, {branch: gh-pages, path: /} curl -sI https://kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/ | head -1 # 200, redirect page to latest/ curl -s https://kokeb-labs.github.io/<repo>/versions.json # [{"version": "dev", "aliases": ["latest"]...}] When something goes wrong ¶ Symptom Cause Docs job fails at "Install the theme" theme_ref names a ref of ci-tools without packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme Old pages still served at the root The first publish has not run yet, or prune_legacy is false Site shows the README rendered by Jekyll Pages source is a branch other than gh-pages , or GitHub Actions API links 404 on the site CASE_SENSE_NAMES differs from when the links were written; set it to NO Lighthouse fails on performance only A heavy image: export SVG, or compress; check the lighthouse-report artifact

docs.text: Versioning and releases ¶ Many repositories call these reusable workflows. When all of them used @main , one bad commit here broke every one of them at once. Versioning exists so that does not happen again. Scheme ¶ Release tags are immutable semver tags: v1.0.0 , v1.1.0 , v1.1.1 , and so on. The moving major tag ( v1 ) always points at the newest v1.x.y release. Callers pin the major tag : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-cpp-lint.yml@v1 They receive fixes and new optional inputs automatically, never a breaking change. A caller that needs to be fully reproducible can pin an exact tag ( @v1.2.0 ) or a commit SHA. - @main is the development line. Its first users are the self-tests in this repository. What is breaking ¶ Anything that can make an existing, correct caller fail: Change Why it breaks A reusable workflow removed or renamed uses: no longer resolves An input removed Callers that pass it get startup_failure An input's type changed Callers that pass the old type get startup_failure An input or secret made required, or a new required one added Callers that do not pass it get startup_failure An output removed Callers that read it get empty values A job needs a permission it did not need before Callers that grant the old set get startup_failure A breaking change needs a major bump ( v1 → v2 ). It is listed under ### Breaking in CHANGELOG.md , under Unreleased or in the new version section. On pull requests, the self-CI ( .github/scripts/check_contract.py ) compares each ru-*.yml with the base branch. It fails if it finds one of these changes and that heading is missing. Everything else is a minor release (new workflow, new optional input, new output) or a patch release (bug fix, action bump, documentation). Deprecating instead of removing ¶ To retire an input within a major: Keep declaring it, so callers that pass it keep starting. Prefix its description with Deprecated: and say what replaces it. Ignore it, or map it onto the replacement. When it is set, emit a ::warning:: that names the replacement. List it under ### Deprecated in the changelog. Remove it in the next major, and list the removal under ### Breaking . Releases come from the changelog ¶ CHANGELOG.md decides what is released. Entries go under ## [Unreleased] as usual. A pull request that should reach callers also moves them to a new version section: python .github/scripts/changelog.py bump patch # or minor, or major That writes ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD with the Unreleased entries under it. When the pull request merges and the self-CI (every self-test and the CI gate) passes on main , release.yml tags vX.Y.Z on the merge commit, publishes the section as the GitHub Release notes and moves vX . A pull request without a new section is merged without a release; its entries wait under Unreleased for the next one. Callers pinned to @v1 therefore get a fix as soon as a pull request asks for its release, and the changelog and the releases never drift apart. The self-CI ( changelog.py check ) fails a pull request whose new section is not the next patch, minor or major, has no date or no entries, leaves entries under Unreleased, or has ### Breaking without being a major. Two pull requests that both add 1.0.6 cannot both merge: the second must be rebased and bumped again. Cutting a release by hand (maintainers) ¶ A tag push still works, for a pre-release or to re-run a release: Make sure CHANGELOG.md has the ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD section on main . Tag the commit and push the tag: git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "v1.0.0" git push origin v1.0.0 release.yml then creates the GitHub Release, with the matching changelog section as notes (generated notes when there is none). If the tag is the highest v1.*.* release, it also force-updates v1 to the same commit. A pre-release tag ( v1.1.0-rc.1 ) gets a pre-release and leaves v1 alone. A patch to an older minor does not move v1 backwards. The release workflow pushes v1 with the workflow token. If a tag ruleset protects v* , allow GitHub Actions to update it, or move the tag by hand. Re-runs use the old revision ¶ Re-run failed jobs reruns the workflow at the revision the original run resolved, including the revision of each reusable workflow. After a fix lands here, or after v1 moves, start a new run instead: push a commit, use Run workflow , or close and reopen the pull request. Keeping callers current ¶ Callers pinned to @v1 need nothing more for minor and patch releases. For majors, and for callers that pin exact tags or SHAs, Dependabot with package-ecosystem: github-actions proposes the update, because it also tracks uses: references to reusable workflows. Inside this repository ¶ The workflows in this repository pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs with a # vX.Y.Z comment. Dependabot ( .github/dependabot.yml ) keeps both current.

On pull requests, the self-CI ( .github/scripts/check_contract.py ) compares each ru-*.yml with the base branch. It fails if it finds one of these changes and that heading is missing. Everything else is a minor release (new workflow, new optional input, new output) or a patch release (bug fix, action bump, documentation).
docs.title: What is breaking

docs.text: To retire an input within a major: Keep declaring it, so callers that pass it keep starting. Prefix its description with Deprecated: and say what replaces it. Ignore it, or map it onto the replacement. When it is set, emit a ::warning:: that names the replacement. List it under ### Deprecated in the changelog. Remove it in the next major, and list the removal under ### Breaking .
docs.title: Deprecating instead of removing

docs.text: CHANGELOG.md decides what is released. Entries go under ## [Unreleased] as usual. A pull request that should reach callers also moves them to a new version section: python .github/scripts/changelog.py bump patch # or minor, or major That writes ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD with the Unreleased entries under it. When the pull request merges and the self-CI (every self-test and the CI gate) passes on main , release.yml tags vX.Y.Z on the merge commit, publishes the section as the GitHub Release notes and moves vX . A pull request without a new section is merged without a release; its entries wait under Unreleased for the next one. Callers pinned to @v1 therefore get a fix as soon as a pull request asks for its release, and the changelog and the releases never drift apart. The self-CI ( changelog.py check ) fails a pull request whose new section is not the next patch, minor or major, has no date or no entries, leaves entries under Unreleased, or has ### Breaking without being a major. Two pull requests that both add 1.0.6 cannot both merge: the second must be rebased and bumped again.
docs.title: Releases come from the changelog

docs.text: A tag push still works, for a pre-release or to re-run a release: Make sure CHANGELOG.md has the ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD section on main . Tag the commit and push the tag: git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "v1.0.0" git push origin v1.0.0 release.yml then creates the GitHub Release, with the matching changelog section as notes (generated notes when there is none). If the tag is the highest v1.*.* release, it also force-updates v1 to the same commit. A pre-release tag ( v1.1.0-rc.1 ) gets a pre-release and leaves v1 alone. A patch to an older minor does not move v1 backwards. The release workflow pushes v1 with the workflow token. If a tag ruleset protects v* , allow GitHub Actions to update it, or move the tag by hand.
docs.title: Cutting a release by hand (maintainers)

docs.text: Re-run failed jobs reruns the workflow at the revision the original run resolved, including the revision of each reusable workflow. After a fix lands here, or after v1 moves, start a new run instead: push a commit, use Run workflow , or close and reopen the pull request.
docs.title: Re-runs use the old revision

docs.text: Callers pinned to @v1 need nothing more for minor and patch releases. For majors, and for callers that pin exact tags or SHAs, Dependabot with package-ecosystem: github-actions proposes the update, because it also tracks uses: references to reusable workflows.
docs.title: Keeping callers current

docs.text: The workflows in this repository pin third-party actions to full commit SHAs with a # vX.Y.Z comment. Dependabot ( .github/dependabot.yml ) keeps both current.

docs.text: dco ¶ Fail a pull request when any of its commits lacks a Signed-off-by: line that matches the commit's author. dco.yml enforces the Developer Certificate of Origin that every Kokeb Labs repository asks of its contributors. It reads the pull request's commits through the GitHub API with actions/github-script ; it checks out nothing, so no code of the pull request runs. What it does ¶ Lists the commits of the pull request (up to 250, the API's limit; a longer pull request fails with a message). Skips merge commits ( skip_merge_commits ) and commits whose GitHub author is a bot ( allow_bots ). Accepts a commit when one of its Signed-off-by: Name <email> trailers has the author's name and email, compared without case and with runs of spaces collapsed. Fails with one error per commit and a table in the job summary: the commit, its subject, and the sign-off it has (or that it has none). On an event without a pull request (a push, merge_group ) it passes with a notice. docs.text: ESP-IDF quickstart ¶ Add an ESP32 build to a repository in three files: the app list, the tools and a fifteen-line workflow. What the workflow expects ¶ File Purpose examples/esp32/CMakeLists.txt The ESP-IDF project: idf.py build works in this folder examples/esp32/app_config.yml The apps to build, with the ESP-IDF versions, build types and target examples/esp32/sdkconfig.defaults Kconfig defaults; Kokeb Labs projects set CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 here examples/esp32/scripts/ espidf-tools as a submodule (or let the workflow clone it) examples/esp32 is the Kokeb Labs convention and the path the matrix script looks in first; see The matrix before you put the project anywhere else. FreeRTOS runs at 1000 Hz Kokeb Labs ESP-IDF projects run FreeRTOS at 1000 Hz; kb-core's RTOS timing assumes at least 1 kHz for ms-precision delays. ESP-IDF's default is 100 Hz. The workflow passes no defaults file of its own, so ESP-IDF reads sdkconfig.defaults from the project folder, and a committed sdkconfig takes precedence over it. Put CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=1000 in whichever of the two the project uses. Add the tools as a submodule: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs/espidf-tools.git examples/esp32/scripts List the apps in examples/esp32/app_config.yml : --- metadata : target : esp32c6 idf_versions : [ "release/v5.5" ] build_types : [[ "Debug" , "Release" ]] apps : gpio_test : description : GPIO self-test source_file : GpioTest.cpp Call the workflow from .github/workflows/esp32-examples-build-ci.yml : --- name : ESP32 examples build on : push : branches : [ main ] pull_request : jobs : build : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : write with : project_dir : examples/esp32 project_tools_dir : examples/esp32/scripts Open a pull request. The run shows one job per app, ESP-IDF version and build type, uploads a fw-<app>-<idf>-<build type> artifact for each and comments a size table on the pull request. Grant the permissions in the calling job A reusable workflow cannot use more permissions than its caller grants. Without pull-requests: write the run fails before any job starts ( startup_failure ). See the permissions contract . Add releases ¶ To attach the firmware to a GitHub Release on every v* tag, add .github/workflows/release.yml : --- name : Release on : push : tags : [ "v*" ] jobs : release : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-with-artifacts.yml@v1 permissions : contents : write with : build_workflow : esp32-examples-build-ci.yml The build must have run on the tagged commit first; see ru-release-with-artifacts . Next: ru-build , every input and what can go wrong.

docs.text: Permissions contract ¶ What each reusable workflow needs from its caller, and the rules that keep that list true. Why it matters ¶ A called workflow cannot have more permissions than its caller grants. When a job of a reusable workflow asks for more, GitHub refuses the whole run before any job starts ( startup_failure ), in every repository that calls it. So a workflow here asks for the least it needs, per job, and the README and this page say exactly what that is. What each workflow needs ¶ Grant at least the "Caller grants" column on the calling job, or at the top of the calling workflow. The table is read from the workflow files. Workflow Caller grants Job: permissions dco.yml contents: read , pull-requests: read dco : contents: read , pull-requests: read org-standard-check.yml contents: read check : contents: read ru-build.yml contents: read , pull-requests: write generate-matrix : contents: read build : contents: read size-report : pull-requests: write ru-ci-gate.yml contents: read gate : contents: read ru-cpp-analysis.yml contents: read cppcheck : contents: read ru-cpp-lint.yml contents: read lint : contents: read ru-cross-build.yml contents: read plan : none build : contents: read ru-docs-linkcheck.yml contents: read link-check : contents: read ru-docs-publish.yml contents: write input-validation : none quality-checks : contents: read version-detection : contents: read build : contents: write ru-handbook-check.yml contents: read check : contents: read ru-host-ci.yml contents: read host : contents: read ru-host-quality.yml contents: read limits : none complexity : contents: read coverage : contents: read sanitizers : contents: read fuzz : contents: read ru-markdown-lint.yml contents: read markdownlint : contents: read ru-mkdocs-publish.yml contents: write build : contents: read quality : contents: read deploy : contents: write ru-release-with-artifacts.yml contents: write release : contents: write ru-release.yml contents: write release : contents: write ru-yaml-lint.yml contents: read yamllint : contents: read The rules ¶ The self-CI ( check_permissions.py in the workflow contract checks job) fails a pull request when: Rule Why A reusable workflow's top-level permissions: is missing or not {} Nothing is granted by default; permissions are per job, so a read-only job never holds a write token A job of a reusable workflow has no permissions: mapping It would inherit everything the caller granted A workflow's job permissions differ from its row in the README table More breaks callers; less means the table asks for too much A reusable workflow has no row, or a row names no workflow The table is the contract callers read A caller in this repository grants less than the contract The self-tests would hit startup_failure A new permission on an existing workflow is a breaking change: it needs a ### Breaking entry in the changelog and a new major ( Versioning ). The "no bare && tail" rule ¶ GitHub runs run: blocks with bash -e , and a script's exit status is that of its last command. A last line such as [ -n "$X" ] && echo "..." fails the step whenever the condition is false, although -e ignores the same line anywhere else. check_run_tails.py fails any run: block that ends that way; write an if ... fi instead. docs.text: ru-build ¶ Build every ESP32 example app of a repository across ESP-IDF versions and build types, upload the firmware and report its size on pull requests. File: .github/workflows/ru-build.yml Caller ¶ --- name : ESP32 examples build on : push : branches : [ main ] pull_request : workflow_dispatch : inputs : clean_build : type : boolean default : false jobs : build : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-build.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read pull-requests : write with : project_dir : examples/esp32 project_tools_dir : examples/esp32/scripts clean_build : ${{ inputs.clean_build || false }} max_dec_total : "0" Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description project_dir string required Path to the ESP-IDF project (contains CMakeLists.txt) project_tools_dir string empty Path to project tools directory (contains scripts directly). Leave empty to auto-detect. clean_build boolean false Skip caches for a clean build. auto_clone_tools boolean true Auto-clone tools repo if project_tools_dir is missing max_dec_total string 0 Maximum total dec size in bytes for size budget enforcement (0 to disable) Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Runs Permissions generate-matrix always contents: read build once per matrix entry, fail-fast: false , 30 min limit contents: read size-report pull requests only pull-requests: write generate-matrix checks out with submodules, finds the project tools (below), runs generate_matrix.py and outputs the matrix. build frees runner disk space, checks out, restores the pip cache (skipped with clean_build ), installs the tools' requirements.txt , pulls espressif/idf:<version> (4 attempts, 10 / 30 / 60 s apart), runs build_app.sh inside the image with espressif/esp-idf-ci-action and uploads the build folder. size-report downloads every fw-* artifact, writes a size table from size.info / size.txt , comments it on the pull request and enforces max_dec_total when it is not 0 . The caller grants the union: contents: read and pull-requests: write . See the permissions contract . Finding the project tools ¶ The generate-matrix job needs generate_matrix.py , build_app.sh and config_loader.sh from espidf-tools . It looks, in this order: Case Path used project_tools_dir set That path; the job fails if it does not exist (no clone) project_tools_dir empty and <project_dir>/espidf-tools exists That folder Otherwise espidf-tools at the repository root, cloned from main (depth 1) when it is missing and auto_clone_tools is true A submodule is the reproducible choice: the clone follows the tools' main branch. The matrix ¶ generate_matrix.py reads app_config.yml and emits one entry per app, ESP-IDF version and build type: app_config.yml Effect metadata.idf_versions ESP-IDF branches or tags, for example release/v5.5 ; default release/v5.5 metadata.build_types One list per IDF version, by index: [["Debug", "Release"], ["Debug"]] metadata.target Chip passed to the build, default esp32c6 apps.<name>.idf_versions , apps.<name>.build_types Per-app overrides; a flat build_types list applies to every version apps.<name>.ci_enabled: false Leaves the app out of CI ci_config.exclude_combinations Entries whose keys all match are dropped, for example {app_name: x, build_type: Release} Where app_config.yml is found The workflow runs generate_matrix.py without --project-path , so the script looks for examples/esp32/app_config.yml from the repository root, then for app_config.yml in the folder above the script. Keep the project in examples/esp32 , or keep the tools inside the project folder, so both point at the same file. Artifacts ¶ Each build uploads <project_dir>/build* as fw-<app_name>-<idf_version_docker>-<build_type> , for example fw-gpio_test-release-v5.5-Debug , kept for 7 days. build_app.sh writes size.info and size.txt into the build folder; the size report reads them. The upload runs even when the build fails, so a failed build's logs are in the artifact. Size report and budget ¶ On pull requests the size-report job comments a table with one row per build (app, IDF, target, build type and the idf.py size summary). Set max_dec_total to a byte count to fail the job when any build's total dec size is larger; 0 turns the check off. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix startup_failure , no job ran The calling job grants less than contents: read , pull-requests: write Add the permissions to the calling job Project tools directory not found project_tools_dir points at a missing folder, or the submodule was not added Add the submodule, or leave project_tools_dir empty to clone Required script ... not found The tools folder is not espidf-tools, or is an old copy Update the submodule Configuration file not found No app_config.yml where generate_matrix.py looks (see the warning above) Move the project to examples/esp32 or the tools into the project Could not pull espressif/idf:... after 4 attempts Docker Hub outage, or an IDF version with no image Check the version name; start a new run No build directory found! build_app.sh failed before creating build* Read the build step log; reproduce locally with build_app.sh Size budget exceeded A build's dec total is above max_dec_total Shrink the firmware or raise the budget A fix here does not apply "Re-run failed jobs" reuses the workflow revision of the first run Start a new run (see Versioning ) Next: ru-release-with-artifacts , which ships these artifacts.

docs.text: ru-ci-gate ¶ One required status check per repository: it passes only when every other CI job passed. ru-ci-gate.yml turns the results of all jobs in a workflow into a single check. A repository's ruleset then requires that one check instead of a list of job names that has to be updated whenever jobs are added, renamed or split. Caller pattern ¶ Add the gate as the last job of the CI workflow: jobs : build : # ... lint : # ... docs : # ... ci-gate : name : CI gate needs : [ build , lint , docs ] # every other job in this workflow if : always() # required, see below uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-ci-gate.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : needs_json : ${{ toJSON(needs) }} allow_skipped : docs # optional: jobs that may be skipped Then, in the repository ruleset (or branch protection), require only the status check named: CI gate / gate GitHub names checks from a called workflow <calling job name> / <called job name> , so with name: CI gate on the calling job the check is always CI gate / gate , in every repository. Rules ¶ The gate passes if and only if every job in needs finished with success , or with skipped and is listed in allow_skipped . failure , cancelled , and an unlisted skipped all fail it. if: always() is required. Without it, a failing job causes the gate to be skipped, and a skipped required check counts as passing . Every job must be in needs . A job outside needs can fail without failing the gate. With verify_needs: true (the default) the gate reads the calling workflow file and fails if either rule above is broken. It also fails if allow_skipped names a job that is not in needs , which catches typos. Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description needs_json string required The caller's needs context as JSON: the expression toJSON(needs) allow_skipped string empty Jobs (ids from needs ) that may be skipped without failing the gate, separated by commas, spaces or newlines. Every other job must succeed. verify_needs boolean true Read the calling workflow file and fail if a job is missing from the gate's needs , or if the gate job lacks if: always() . Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps gate (gate) contents: read Evaluate needed jobs contents: read is used to read the calling workflow file. Jobs that run conditionally ¶ A job that is skipped by design, for example a deploy job that runs only on main , goes in allow_skipped . A job that is skipped because something it needs failed is reported as skipped too. That case is still caught: the failed upstream job is itself in needs , so the gate fails on it.

docs.text: ru-cpp-analysis ¶ Run cppcheck over source folders, without a build, and keep the report as an artifact. ru-cpp-analysis.yml runs cppcheck in a container ( ghcr.io/facthunder/cppcheck ) over paths . It needs no compile database, so it suits header-only drivers and repositories without a host build; with a CMake build, ru-host-ci runs cppcheck on the compiler's own database instead. What it does ¶ Checks out the repository. Runs cppcheck with --enable=<enable> , --std=<std> , inline suppressions, -i for each exclude path, and --force / --max-configs when set. missingIncludeSystem and unmatchedSuppression are suppressed, because system headers are not mounted. Uploads cppcheck_report.xml and the console output as the cppcheck-report artifact (14 days). With strict: true , fails the job when the report is not empty. Caller ¶ jobs : cppcheck : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-cpp-analysis.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : paths : "src inc" std : c++20 strict : true Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps cppcheck contents: read actions/checkout ; Install cppcheck; Run cppcheck; Upload report; Fail on findings (strict) Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description paths string src inc examples Dirs to analyze (space-separated) std string c++20 C++ standard strict boolean false Fail the job when cppcheck reports a finding (severity other than information) exclude string empty Paths to exclude (space-separated) enable string warning,style,performance,portability,information Checks to enable (comma-separated: all,warning,style,performance, portability,information,unusedFunction,missingInclude) force boolean false Force checking even with incomplete analysis max_configs number 0 Maximum configs to check (for template-heavy code, 0=unlimited) artifact_name string cppcheck-report Name of the uploaded report artifact (unique per call when a run calls this more than once) When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix The job passes although cppcheck printed findings strict is false (the default) Set strict: true once the findings are fixed "Too many #ifdef configurations" Template- or macro-heavy code Set max_configs , or force: true A path is not found paths and exclude are relative to the repository root, space-separated Check each folder exists in the checkout

docs.text: ru-cpp-lint ¶ Check C and C++ formatting with clang-format and lint with clang-tidy, with results as annotations on the pull request. ru-cpp-lint.yml runs clang-format 20.1.8 and clang-tidy 20.1.0 with the repository's own .clang-format and .clang-tidy . Both come from LLVM's builds published on PyPI, pinned and checked against their SHA-256, so no install script or third-party action runs. With cmake_args , it configures the project first and gives clang-tidy the CMake compile database, so clang-tidy sees the include paths and defines the compiler sees; without it, clang-tidy guesses and cannot find the project's own headers. Every finding fails the job unless fail_on_findings is false. What it does ¶ Checks out the repository. Links clang_format_config and clang_tidy_config to .clang-format and .clang-tidy at the root when they live elsewhere (the Kokeb Labs layout keeps them in _config/ ). A missing file is a warning, not an error. Installs the pinned clang-format and clang-tidy. Selects the files: git ls-files with extensions , without ignore , and only the files a pull request changes when files_changed_only is true. With cmake_args , configures CMake with CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON into build-clang-tidy/ . Runs clang-format ( --dry-run -Werror ) and clang-tidy on every selected file in parallel. Each finding is an annotation on its line; the run summary has a table and the clang-tidy findings. Compiler warnings that clang-tidy echoes as clang-diagnostic-* are left to the build, except hard errors. Fails when any file has a finding ( fail_on_findings , default true). findings is the number of such files. thread_comments and lines_changed_only are still accepted but ignored: whole files are always checked. Caller ¶ jobs : lint : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-cpp-lint.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : clang_format_config : _config/.clang-format clang_tidy_config : _config/.clang-tidy files_changed_only : true Jobs and permissions ¶ Job Permissions Steps lint contents: read actions/checkout ; Prepare clang configuration; Install clang-format and clang-tidy (pinned, hash-checked); Select files; Configure for clang-tidy (compile_commands.json); clang-format and clang-tidy; Fail on findings The job needs only contents: read : annotations come from the log, and nothing is posted to the pull request. Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description clang_version string 20 Clang major version of clang-format and clang-tidy (20 is the supported version) clang_format_config string _config/.clang-format Path to clang-format configuration file clang_tidy_config string _config/.clang-tidy Path to clang-tidy configuration file tidy_checks string empty clang-tidy checks (comma-separated glob patterns, use - prefix to disable) extensions string c,cpp,cc,cxx,h,hpp,ipp,tpp,inl File extensions to check (comma-separated) ignore string build|.git Files or directories to exclude from linting (pipe-separated) files_changed_only boolean false Only lint files that have been changed in the pull request lines_changed_only boolean false Deprecated, ignored: whole files are always checked, which is stricter. Kept so existing callers do not break. step_summary boolean true Add a summary of linting results to the workflow step summary file_annotations boolean true Display linting errors and warnings as file annotations in the GitHub UI thread_comments boolean false Deprecated, ignored: findings are reported as annotations and in the run summary. Kept so existing callers do not break. cmake_args string empty Arguments for a CMake configure that exports compile_commands.json for clang-tidy (for example "-DMYCHIP_BUILD_TESTS=ON"). Without a compile database clang-tidy cannot see the project's include paths and reports "file not found" for its own headers. Empty: no configure, no database. cmake_source_dir string . Directory with the top-level CMakeLists.txt for the cmake_args configure fail_on_findings boolean true Fail the job when clang-format or clang-tidy reports a finding. Set false to only report (the count is in the findings output). When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix clang-tidy reports file not found for the project's own headers No compile database Set cmake_args so CMake exports one Every line of a file is reported by clang-format The config was not found, so the default style was used Check the clang_format_config path; the log says which file was linked clang-tidy reports missing headers No compile database: include paths are guessed Use ru-host-ci for clang-tidy, keep this for formatting Findings in vendored code The folder is not in ignore Add it, pipe-separated: build|.git|third_party

docs.text: ru-handbook-check ¶ Check a repository against the Kokeb Labs handbook rules that a script can decide, and report every finding by rule ID. The declaration ¶ Each repository says what it is in .kokeb/handbook.yml : --- handbook : "1.0" # the handbook release it follows kind : driver # driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs or template level : high # standard, high or safety waivers : # optional - rule : KB-DOC-004 reason : Doxygen comments for the v2 register API land with #41. approved_by : "@N3b3x" until : 2027-01-31 A rule applies when the repository's kind is in the rule's scope and its level is at or above the rule's lowest level. What it checks ¶ Rule Check KB-REPO-002 The declaration exists and names a handbook release, a kind and a level KB-REPO-003 Every waiver names a handbook rule, a reason, an approver and a date that has not passed KB-REPO-005 The root of a driver holds only the committed entries ADR-0011 allows KB-REPO-018 driver.yml has name, version, bus, mcus, peripheral and kb_core_min, matching cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake KB-CPP-001 The library requires C++20 and compiler extensions are not turned on KB-BLD-002 No file(GLOB) in CMake outside tests/ and examples/ KB-CPP-002 No throw , try , catch , typeid or dynamic_cast in inc/ and src/ KB-CPP-003 No new , delete , malloc and friends, or heap-owning smart pointers in inc/ and src/ KB-ARCH-011 No virtual in a driver (ADR-0016) KB-CPP-012 Driver headers include only the target library subset; other target code includes no allocating, throwing or OS header (ADR-0017) KB-REPO-016 No generated sdkconfig is committed (ADR-0018) KB-DOC-035 No PDF is committed under docs/ (ADR-0019) Code checks read only committed files, with comments and string literals blanked out first, so a word in a comment or a message never counts. = delete and placement new are not heap use. How a finding counts ¶ Error (fails the job): the rule is active, or its enforce_from date has passed. Warning : the rule is still proposed and its enforce_from date is ahead, or it is a should rule. Notice : a valid waiver covers the rule; the notice quotes the waiver. Each finding is an annotation on its file and line with the rule's ID, title and a link to its page, and the run summary has the full table. Where the rules come from ¶ The checker and rules.json , a snapshot of the handbook's rules exported by the handbook's own tooling, live in tools/handbook_check/ in this repository. The workflow checks them out at its own commit, so a caller on @v1 always gets a checker and a rule set that belong together. docs.text: Each repository says what it is in .kokeb/handbook.yml : --- handbook : "1.0" # the handbook release it follows kind : driver # driver, library, hal, firmware, tooling, docs or template level : high # standard, high or safety waivers : # optional - rule : KB-DOC-004 reason : Doxygen comments for the v2 register API land with #41. approved_by : "@N3b3x" until : 2027-01-31 A rule applies when the repository's kind is in the rule's scope and its level is at or above the rule's lowest level.
docs.title: The declaration

docs.text: Rule Check KB-REPO-002 The declaration exists and names a handbook release, a kind and a level KB-REPO-003 Every waiver names a handbook rule, a reason, an approver and a date that has not passed KB-REPO-005 The root of a driver holds only the committed entries ADR-0011 allows KB-REPO-018 driver.yml has name, version, bus, mcus, peripheral and kb_core_min, matching cmake/<chip>_build_settings.cmake KB-CPP-001 The library requires C++20 and compiler extensions are not turned on KB-BLD-002 No file(GLOB) in CMake outside tests/ and examples/ KB-CPP-002 No throw , try , catch , typeid or dynamic_cast in inc/ and src/ KB-CPP-003 No new , delete , malloc and friends, or heap-owning smart pointers in inc/ and src/ KB-ARCH-011 No virtual in a driver (ADR-0016) KB-CPP-012 Driver headers include only the target library subset; other target code includes no allocating, throwing or OS header (ADR-0017) KB-REPO-016 No generated sdkconfig is committed (ADR-0018) KB-DOC-035 No PDF is committed under docs/ (ADR-0019) Code checks read only committed files, with comments and string literals blanked out first, so a word in a comment or a message never counts. = delete and placement new are not heap use.
docs.title: What it checks

docs.text: Error (fails the job): the rule is active, or its enforce_from date has passed. Warning : the rule is still proposed and its enforce_from date is ahead, or it is a should rule. Notice : a valid waiver covers the rule; the notice quotes the waiver. Each finding is an annotation on its file and line with the rule's ID, title and a link to its page, and the run summary has the full table.
docs.title: How a finding counts

docs.text: The checker and rules.json , a snapshot of the handbook's rules exported by the handbook's own tooling, live in tools/handbook_check/ in this repository. The workflow checks them out at its own commit, so a caller on @v1 always gets a checker and a rule set that belong together.

docs.text: ru-host-ci ¶ Build, test and analyse a CMake project on the host, with clang-tidy 18 and cppcheck over the compiler's own compile database. ru-host-ci.yml runs the native (host) half of a C/C++ project's CI in one job: Configure. Uses cmake --preset <preset> when preset is set, otherwise cmake -S <source_dir> -B <build_dir> -G Ninja . Either way it passes -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON . Build. Runs cmake --build <build_dir> --parallel . Test. Runs ctest --test-dir <build_dir> --output-on-failure . Select files. Picks translation units from compile_commands.json . A unit is analysed if its path relative to the repository root matches tidy_paths . Units that match exclude_paths and anything generated in the build tree are dropped. The selection is written as a filtered database, so both analysers see exactly the same files. Analyse. Runs clang-tidy 18 ( -p <build_dir> ) and cppcheck ( --project=<filtered database> ) on that set. Both see the include paths and defines the compiler sees, so no configuration is guessed. Report. Findings appear as annotations. The reports, the file list and the database are uploaded as an artifact. With fail_on_findings: true (the default), any finding fails the job. clang-tidy exits 0 even when it prints warnings, so the workflow counts file:line:col: warning|error: ... [check] lines itself. It ignores compiler warnings echoed as clang-diagnostic-* , except clang-diagnostic-error . cppcheck findings are lines of severity error, warning, performance, portability or style; information lines (analysis limits) do not count. Empty: configure with -S source_dir -B build_dir. source_dir string . CMake source directory, relative to the repository root build_dir string build/host Build directory, relative to the repository root. With a preset this must be the preset's binaryDir; compile_commands.json is read from here. cmake_args string empty Extra arguments for the configure step (space separated) build_type string Debug CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE when no preset is used run_tests boolean true Run ctest after the build ctest_args string empty Extra arguments for ctest (space separated) tidy_paths string empty Python regular expression matched (re.search) against each translation unit's path relative to the repository root. Only matching files are given to clang-tidy and cppcheck. Empty: every file in the database. exclude_paths string (^|/)(third_party|external|vendor|_deps)/ Python regular expression; translation units whose relative path matches are never analysed, and findings in matching files are not counted. The build directory is always excluded. run_clang_tidy boolean true Run clang-tidy 18 on the selected files clang_tidy_config string empty Path to a .clang-tidy file. Empty: clang-tidy's normal lookup from each source file run_cppcheck boolean true Run cppcheck on the selected files cppcheck_suppressions string empty Path to a cppcheck --suppressions-list file (optional) cppcheck_enable string warning,performance,portability cppcheck --enable value fail_on_findings boolean true Fail the job when clang-tidy or cppcheck report findings apt_packages string empty Extra apt packages to install before configuring (space separated) submodules string false actions/checkout submodules value: false, true or recursive runs_on string ubuntu-24.04 Runner label (Ubuntu 24.04 or newer, for clang-tidy-18 from apt) artifact_name string host-ci-reports Name of the uploaded report artifact Outputs: tidy_findings and cppcheck_findings , the counts of findings (empty when a tool did not run). docs.text: ru-host-quality ¶ Complexity, coverage and sanitizer gates for a CMake C/C++ project, with the limits the Kokeb Labs handbook sets for each assurance level (ADR-0020). ru-host-quality.yml runs three independent jobs: Job Tool Measures Fails when complexity lizard 1.24.1 Modified cyclomatic complexity (a whole switch counts once), lines of code and parameters of every function in library_paths a function is over a limit coverage GCC 14 --coverage , gcovr 8.7 Line, branch and, when the level asks for it, MC/DC coverage ( -fcondition-coverage ) of library_paths by the tests a figure is below its floor sanitizers clang, AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer The tests built with -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all any report, or a failing test Python tools are installed from pinned versions checked against their SHA-256 hashes, and each version was at least three weeks old when it was pinned. Limits by level ¶ Limit standard high safety Cyclomatic complexity (modified) 15 15 10 Function length (lines of code) 80 60 60 Parameters 7 6 6 Line coverage reported 85% 100% Branch coverage reported 75% 100% MC/DC coverage not measured reported 100% Every limit can be overridden with an input ( max_ccn , max_length , max_params , min_line , min_branch , min_condition ); an override should match a waiver or deviation recorded in the repository. What is counted ¶ Library code only. library_paths (default inc src ) names it. Tests, examples and tools are not measured for complexity and do not count towards coverage. Every C and C++ file, header-only implementations included. The complexity job lists .c , .cc , .cpp , .cxx , .h , .hh , .hpp , .hxx , .ipp , .tpp and .inl files under library_paths itself: lizard alone skips .ipp , .tpp and .inl files in a directory, which is where a header-only driver keeps its code. Per source line, all template instances together. A header-only driver is a class template, compiled once for every port type a test or example uses. gcovr's --merge-lines counts a line, branch or condition as covered when any instance ran it: coverage measures the source, as a structural-coverage objective does, not how many copies the compiler made. Without it, an example that instantiates the driver with its own port and runs only the happy path would count every failure path a second time, as uncovered. Only code that ran. Coverage reads the data of test binaries that executed. A compile-only target (for example an optimised build that exists to prove the code compiles at -O2 ) has no data and would otherwise count every line as missed. No exception branches. The compiler's exception-handling branches and unreachable branches are excluded: Kokeb code builds without exceptions. Minimal caller ¶ jobs : quality : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-host-quality.yml@v1 permissions : contents : read with : level : high cmake_args : "-DMYCHIP_BUILD_TESTS=ON" Add the job to the CI gate's needs . The reports (lizard's full table, gcovr's HTML, Cobertura XML and JSON summary) are uploaded as artifacts, and the figures appear in the run summary. Outputs ¶ complexity_findings , line_coverage , branch_coverage and condition_coverage let a later job record the figures, for example in a release's evidence package.

docs.text: ru-mkdocs-publish ¶ Build, check, audit and publish a Kokeb Labs documentation site with the shared theme, versioned or not. ru-mkdocs-publish.yml builds a Kokeb Labs documentation site with the shared theme, checks it, audits it and publishes it to gh-pages as a versioned site with mike , with the Doxygen API reference under api/ . Migrating to MkDocs moves a repository onto it; the style guide says what its pages contain. Where the theme comes from ¶ The theme, the plugin, figkit and the pinned toolchain are the kokeb-mkdocs-theme package in packages/kokeb-mkdocs-theme . Every job installs it with pip from the commit this workflow runs from (the job context's workflow_repository and workflow_sha ), so a caller pinned to @v1 builds with the theme released in v1 , and a branch under review builds with that branch's theme. theme_ref overrides the ref. A repository's own requirements-docs.txt , if it has one, is installed afterwards for extra plugins. What runs when ¶ Event Build + checks Lighthouse + screenshots Publish Pull request Yes Yes Never, whatever deploy says Push to the default branch Yes Yes Version dev (when deploy is true); dev also holds latest until the first release Push of a vX.Y.Z tag Yes Yes Version vX.Y.Z ( release_version: minor : X.Y ), and latest moves to it With versioning: false (the organisation portal) there are no versions: see Unversioned sites . The site root redirects to latest . Aliases are symlinks, so the API reference added to a version folder is reachable through them too. Material's version selector in the header lists every version. Jobs and permissions ¶ The caller grants contents: write , even one that never publishes (pull requests, deploy: false ): GitHub checks the permissions of every job of a called workflow before the run starts, whatever the job's if . Job Permissions Steps build contents: read Check out (plus submodule_paths ), install the theme, run check_commands ( kokeb-docs check ), mkdocs build --strict , Doxygen into api/ (with the Kokeb Labs API stylesheet when the Doxyfile has none), lychee --offline --include-fragments on the merged site, upload docs-site quality contents: read Lighthouse CI (median of 3 runs, mobile emulation) on the home page and the first navigation pages against lighthouse_budgets , upload lighthouse-report ; Playwright screenshots at 375 and 1280 px, light and dark, upload docs-screenshots deploy contents: write Versioned: prune the pre-MkDocs site from gh-pages ( prune_legacy ), mike deploy , add the API reference to the version folder, mike set-default latest , root 404.html , push (never force). Unversioned: kokeb-docs publish-root commits the built site as the whole branch, push (never force) Every action is pinned to a commit SHA with its version in a comment. The first publish ¶ A repository with an older (Jekyll / Doxygen) site on gh-pages : everything at the top of the branch that is not a mike version or alias is removed in one commit before mike writes (kept: versions.json , index.html once mike owns it, 404.html , .nojekyll , CNAME , robots.txt ). A repository without gh-pages : mike creates the branch. In both cases the root gets mike's redirect to latest/ and a 404.html that sends old addresses to the same page under latest/ ( /docs/x/ , /development/x/ to latest/x/ ; /doxs/ , /html/ to latest/api/ ). Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description python_version string 3.12 Python used to build the site. requirements string requirements-docs.txt Optional pip requirements file installed after the theme package (extra MkDocs plugins). Skipped when the file does not exist; the theme package already pins mkdocs, mkdocs-material, awesome-nav, pymdown and mike. theme_ref string empty Ref of kokeb-labs/ci-tools to install the theme package from. Empty: the commit this workflow runs from, so the theme always matches the workflow. mkdocs_config string mkdocs.yml Path of the site configuration. A repository that keeps tool configuration out of its root passes _config/mkdocs.yml (with docs_dir: ../docs); the theme then takes the folder that holds docs_dir as the repository root (snippets, repository links, figures) and the check commands get it as KOKEB_DOCS_CONFIG. submodules string false Submodules to check out with the repository: 'false', 'true' (top level) or 'recursive'. submodule_paths string empty Space-separated submodule paths to initialise (shallow) after checkout, nested ones included: each parent submodule on the way is initialised without recursion, e.g. 'lib/core/drivers/internal/pincfg'. Use it instead of 'recursive' when the checks need a few nested submodules. check_commands string if [ -f tools/figkit/build.py ]; then python3 tools/figkit/build.py --check; fi if [ -f tools/docs/gen.py ]; then python3 tools/docs/gen.py --check; fi if [ ! -f tools/figkit/build.py ] && [ ! -f tools/docs/gen.py ]; then kokeb-docs check; fi Shell lines run before the build, with GH_TOKEN set to the job's read-only token (for commands that read the GitHub API); any failure fails the job. The default runs the figure drift check and the generated-region check (kokeb-docs check), or a repository's own tools/figkit and tools/docs/gen.py when it still carries them. doxygen_config string empty Doxyfile for the API reference, relative to doxygen_working_directory. Empty: no API. doxygen_working_directory string . Directory Doxygen runs in; relative paths in the Doxyfile resolve against it. doxygen_html_dir string empty Directory of the generated HTML, relative to doxygen_working_directory. Empty: read OUTPUT_DIRECTORY and HTML_OUTPUT from the Doxyfile. api_dir string api Folder of the site that receives the Doxygen HTML (match extra.api_dir in mkdocs.yml). link_check boolean true Run lychee offline on the built site (internal links, anchors and images, API included). link_check_args string empty Extra lychee arguments, for example --exclude-path patterns. lighthouse boolean true Run Lighthouse on the built site (home page and the first navigation pages) against the budgets. lighthouse_budgets string performance=0.8 accessibility=0.95 best-practices=0.9 seo=0.9 Minimum Lighthouse category scores (0-1, median of three runs, mobile emulation), space-separated category=score pairs. docs.text: ru-release-with-artifacts ¶ Create a GitHub Release for a tag and attach the firmware that ru-build built and tested for the same commit. File: .github/workflows/ru-release-with-artifacts.yml Caller ¶ --- name : Release on : push : tags : [ "v*" ] jobs : release : uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-with-artifacts.yml@v1 permissions : contents : write with : build_workflow : esp32-examples-build-ci.yml fail_on_no_artifacts : true Release only after CI passed on the tag ¶ Triggered by the tag push itself, the release runs at the same time as CI on that tag and can publish before (or without) a green build. Trigger it from the finished CI run instead, and pass the tag and the commit: on : workflow_run : workflows : [ CI ] types : [ completed ] permissions : contents : write jobs : release : if : >- github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' && startsWith(github.event.workflow_run.head_branch, 'v') uses : kokeb-labs/ci-tools/.github/workflows/ru-release-with-artifacts.yml@v1 with : build_workflow : ci.yml tag_name : ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }} commit : ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }} fail_on_no_artifacts : true The workflow checks that the tag points to commit before it releases anything. Inputs ¶ Input Type Default Description build_workflow string esp32-examples-build-ci.yml Name of the ESP32 build workflow artifact_pattern string fw-.* Pattern for firmware artifacts draft boolean false Create as draft release prerelease boolean false Mark as pre-release tag_name string empty Tag name for release (defaults to github.ref_name) fail_on_no_artifacts boolean false Fail if no firmware artifacts found commit string empty Commit whose CI artifacts are released, and that the release tag must point to. Empty: github.sha. A caller triggered by workflow_run passes github.event.workflow_run.head_sha, because github.sha is then the default branch's head, not the tagged commit. Jobs and permissions ¶ One job, release , with contents: write . It checks out with full history, downloads every artifact whose name matches artifact_pattern from the run of build_workflow on github.sha ( dawidd6/action-download-artifact ), builds the release files with tools/release_assets/release_assets.py from ci-tools at the same commit as this workflow, and creates the release for tag_name (default: the pushed tag) with generated notes and those files attached ( softprops/action-gh-release ). The checksums also go to the run's summary. The workflow does not ask for actions: read : existing callers grant only contents: write , and the token can read artifacts of its own repository without it. What the release holds ¶ For tag v1.2.0 of a repository whose driver.yml names it as5047u : File What it is as5047u-1.2.0.tar.gz The tagged tree ( git archive ), compressed with a fixed date: the same tag always gives the same bytes. GitHub's own "Source code" archives are not promised to be byte-stable, so checksums name this one. Submodules are not inside; the SBOM names each at its pinned commit. as5047u-1.2.0.spdx.json SBOM, SPDX 2.3 JSON: the repository as the main package (licence from LICENSE , the archive's SHA-256, the tagged commit), each git submodule as a package it contains (URL and pinned commit), and each firmware zip as a file generated from it. fw-<app>-<idf>-<type>.zip One per firmware artifact: for each ESP-IDF build in it, flasher_args.json , flash_args , every file they flash (bootloader, partition table, app) and the app's .elf and .map , at their build paths. An artifact with no flasher_args.json is zipped whole, with a warning. SHA256SUMS SHA-256 of every other file, in sha256sum -c format. One zip per artifact keeps Debug and Release apart. Uploading the build folders file by file, as versions before 1.7.0 did, attached thousands of files (an ESP-IDF build folder holds about 1,500), let files with the same name in Debug and Release overwrite each other, and could pass GitHub's limit of 1,000 files per release. Check a download ¶ gh release download v1.2.0 -R kokeb-labs/driver-as5047u -D v1.2.0 cd v1.2.0 && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS Every line must say OK . To flash a firmware zip: unzip it, go to the build folder inside and run esptool.py --chip <chip> write_flash @flash_args (the chip is in flasher_args.json ). Provenance ¶ The release does not yet carry signed build provenance. GitHub artifact attestations ( actions/attest-build-provenance ) need a public repository, or GitHub Enterprise Cloud for a private one, and an extra id-token: write and attestations: write grant from every caller. They are added when the repositories are public; until then SHA256SUMS and the SBOM tie the files to the tagged commit, and the tag check above ties the firmware to the CI run that tested it. When it finds no firmware ¶ The release only reuses artifacts; it never builds. It finds none when: the build workflow has not run on the tagged commit (tag a commit that was pushed to a branch the build runs on, and wait for that build to finish); the artifacts expired ( ru-build keeps them 7 days); build_workflow names a different file than the caller of ru-build ; artifact_pattern (a regular expression, default fw-.* ) does not match. With fail_on_no_artifacts: false (the default) the release is still created, without firmware, and the step logs a warning. Set it to true to fail instead. When it fails ¶ Symptom Cause Fix startup_failure The calling job does not grant contents: write Grant it in the calling job Resource not accessible by integration when creating the release The repository restricts the workflow token to read Grant contents: write in the caller; check Settings > Actions > Workflow permissions Release has no firmware zips See above Set fail_on_no_artifacts: true to catch it release files share a name Two artifacts would give zips with the same name Give the artifacts distinct names ( ru-build names them by app, IDF version and build type) flasher_args.json lists files the artifact lacks The build artifact was uploaded without part of the build Upload the whole build folder in ru-build tag ... does not exist here The release ran for a tag that was not pushed Push the tag first Next: ensure-tools-directory , for your own jobs that need the project tools.

docs.text: ru-yaml-lint ¶ Lint YAML files with yamllint against the repository's own rules. ru-yaml-lint.yml installs yamllint and runs it on every file matched by paths (comma-separated globs) that is not excluded by exclude_patterns , with config_file when it exists (yamllint's defaults otherwise). docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs kokeb-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. From push to release ¶ From push to release Figure description and sources Two lanes, each read left to right. The top lane runs on every push and pull request: the caller's esp32-examples-build-ci.yml calls ru-build, whose generate-matrix job checks out espidf-tools and turns app_config.yml into a matrix, whose build job runs once per matrix entry in the espressif/idf image, and whose size-report job comments a size table on pull requests. The build job uploads one fw-* artifact per entry. The bottom lane runs when a version tag is pushed: the caller's release.yml calls ru-release-with-artifacts, which downloads those artifacts for the tagged commit and attaches them to a GitHub Release, so nothing is rebuilt. Solid arrows mean "runs next", dashed arrows carry files. Job names are read from the workflow files.
